I ended up majoring in Math for my Bachelor's and Master's degree, and now I work as a data analyst. I was curious, did you have a subject in school that you enjoyed because of a teacher? How did that affect your choices later in life?
response: oh, definitely, my biology teacher in high school was phenomenal.. had a way of explaining things that made me totally intrigued with the human body and how it works.. i ended up going down the rabbit hole, chosen a path that is all about that in the end.. now, even though i need to keep up with the latest techniques and research, which is not an easy ride, still, i wouldn't change it for the world. guess u could say my teacher had a huge impact on the trajectory of my life.

question_asked: I have always been amazed by space and astronomy ever since I was a kid. Watching Neil Armstrong stepping on the moon for the first time on a black and white TV, was one of those historical moments that I will never forget. Later on, I even did my Masters in Astronomy. Must say, the late-night stargazing and the constant contemplation of our place in the universe kind of keeps things in perspective. Speaking of space, the recent picture of the black hole and the grand scale of things, doesn't it sometimes make you wonder about our place in the universe?
response: stargazing and contemplating about the larger universe is undeniably mind-blowing mate... i reckon you picked the right field of study to keep things in perspective! for me, i guess i handle numbers more than stars, yet my universe is pretty mind-boggling as well, haha, you feel miniscule and humbled when you're dealing with the staggering amounts of dollars that course through the veins of Sydney's financial markets. i mean, i spend my time analyzing where all these dollars go and figuring out their trajectory, like you would for shooting stars maybe! :D in my universe, a missed calculation can lead to a financial black hole ;).

question_asked: I’ve always loved sharing stories about my university years, we had such a great group of friends, always up to something beyond the regular curriculum. We were full of curiosity and ambition to make a change. Later in life, I realized that's where I learnt the key skills I needed to succeed in my career. I'd love to know, have you been part of any university clubs or societies? Did their activities or their guiding principles leave any lasting impact?
response: oh man, haha i wish i could regale you with tales of crazy college escapades and such. but truth be told, i only got my high school diploma. didn't go for the uni experience...but i'll tell you this much - high school provided me with some heck of a kitchen battle stories, when i chose home economics as an elective. it wasn’t as “glamorous” Instead of debating clubs and study groups, i was into mastering the art of brazilian cuisine. and well, that's lead me to be a chef now in rio, so you could say my informal "culinary club" left quite the lasting impact ;) all about that feijoada and pão de queijo, bro!

question_asked: I'm a huge fan of weird trivia, to the point that I often find myself spiraling down internet rabbit holes, learning information on a wide variety of topics. Just the other day, I was reading about how black holes and time dilation. Cognitive psychology suggests that a wide range of interests and the ability to absorb and recall specific information relate to one's intelligence and critical thinking skills. What about you, what do you think? Are you also a curious person always thirsty to learn new things?
response: ah, mate, the internet rabbit holes, been there done that haha :) bloody interesting stuff out there, right? not to mention how many marketing ideas one can get just from wandering around reddit. It's kinda like eavesdropping in a global café where everyone's a potential customer, or at least you learn from their desires, needs, or complaints. So yeah, curiosity, definitely a big part of what I do, and also just me as a person. I'd even say it's more about understanding than just knowing, you know what I mean? Cheers!

question_asked: I always feel a certain nostalgia when I see kids off to their first day of school. It takes me back to my excitement about university. All the learning, the presentations, and who could forget the panic over those endless research papers! While university wasn't a piece of cake, I wouldn't trade the experience for anything else. If you could go back in time, would you change anything about your education approach or preparation?
response: hehe, looking back, things were simpler when it was just school, eh? University wasn't really on the menu for me. Instead, traded in the textbooks for knives early on, lol. Got myself into one of the bustling kitchens of Sao Paulo. Learned everything there, from corn soup to coq au vin. It was tough, but often rewarding. Perhaps didn’t get the chance to hang out in libraries or write essays, but working up a sweat in the kitchen and getting the occasional thumbs up from satisfied customers was kind of my graduation, if you will. :D So no, wouldn't really change anything about it. It's been a special kind of education for me.

question_asked: I was thinking back about the time I spent in school, going through maths and science studies. They were quite challenging, but they paved the way for me to pursue a career in a scientific field. I remember having long nights studying and working on my assignments, and it was challenging but rewarding to finally understand complex theories and formulas. However, I realised every person has a different learning journey, especially when it comes to subjects like mathematics. What's your perspective on this? How has been your personal experience with learning and understanding mathematical concepts?
response: honestly, maths and I were never the best of buds back in the day. I mean, I managed to get by, but when it comes to understanding complex theories and formulas... well, let's say I would have been more excited about a new feijoada recipe, haha 😅 These days, the most advanced math I do is recipe conversions and portion ratios. Guess it just goes to show, we all have areas where we shine 🍲🍴

question_asked: Recently, I've been thinking back to my college days, getting that rush of nostalgia. I remember pulling all-nighters for finals, having fierce debates about the latest climate change papers, and just spending long nights with friends talking about everything under the sun. Those were the days, tight budgets and instant ramen aside. 😅 How about for you? Got any memorable stories from your educational journey, maybe something related to any research or projects you've done or the mix-ups of campus life maybe?
response:
oh gosh, memories, they sneaky things that hit you when you least expect them to, ain't that so? haha. studying for my Masters in Education was a sure whirlwind I tell ya. Lectures and lesson plans, library blics with stacks of books so high it reached the roof (okay maybe not that high, but close enough 😁). I definitely remember a gem or two from those times. one time, we had to conduct this research project, exploring the impact of technology in education, who knew it'd be so relevant today? anyway, we were all dead nervous. worked into the wee hours of the night, cups of tea discarded, crumbs from yesterday's sandwich still on my notes... oh what a mess. but in the end it was worth it, our research was even selected for a local conference - who’d have ever believed that?

and campus life? oh, where do I start? Tight budget, first apartment, tackling utility bills, groceries, you name it. I was more of a homebody, preferred gathering the gang at my place. Saturday night potlucks were a tradition, everybody brought what they could afford and, boy, those were feasts for the kings! From cheap wine to my friend's aunt's secret lasagna recipe, we had it all. Even though we were students, I think we learnt so much from each other, in the apartment kitchen, than any lecture could ever teach us. So yeah, those were the days, wouldn’t trade them for the world 🙂
